item.title: Putin says talks must focus on security for Russia, Ukraine and Europe overall
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday that future talks on a settlement of the war in Ukraine should focus on security guarantees for both countries and an overall framework for security throughout Europe.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday that future talks on a settlement of the war in Ukraine should focus on security guarantees for both countries and an overall framework for security throughout Europe. Putin, interviewed on Russian television a day after meeting US presidential envoy Steve Witkoff, confirmed that Russia was ready to resume US-mediated talks with Ukraine next month. He restated longstanding Kremlin policy that Russia never wanted to launch a war, but had run into hostile reactions from Ukraine on key issues of concern to Moscow. Talks on a variety of matters could lead to a positive outcome, he said, but Russia remained intent on a solution ending the conflict rather than a short-lived ceasefire. "The goal of these talks will be to ensure the security of Ukraine and Russia after reaching peace agreements, in their final form, not as a result of a temporary ceasefire for some short period of time. We are ready to resume these contacts to achieve this goal," Putin said. The Russian president said Witkoff also stressed that discussions had to extend to "the architecture of European security as a whole. And I agree with that too. Well, let's see how things develop in the coming days." Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who met Witkoff in Norway on Tuesday, said Ukraine was [USN:L1N4670ZQ TEXT:"ready for talks"] likely to take place by early next month. Ukraine, he said, supported "any proposals for a ceasefire, an end to the war, an energy ceasefire as well as humanitarian initiatives". Efforts headed by the United States to pursue talks stalled in February with the outbreak of the US-Israeli conflict with Iran. Many of the Ukraine war issues focus on territory, with Russia demanding Ukraine cede all of eastern Ukraine's Donbas region. Kyiv rejects any notion of giving up land it currently holds. In his comments, Putin said any discussion on territory in eastern Ukraine had to consider what he said was the fact that the area was "historically Russian land". And residents there, he said, had voted to be a part of Russia in referendums staged seven months after Moscow launched its invasion. "Firstly, my attitude on this matter is that this is not their territory. It’s the territory of historical Russia," he said.

item.title: Brandon Woodruff recovery leaves Brewers with tough call before Game 1
item.description: MILWAUKEE -- After almost a decade as a franchise cornerstone, Milwaukee Brewers right-hander Brandon Woodruff hopes his comeback from his latest injury leads to a spot on the club's 2026 World Series roster.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: MILWAUKEE -- After almost a decade as a franchise cornerstone, Milwaukee Brewers right-hander Brandon Woodruff hopes his comeback from his latest injury leads to a spot on the club's 2026 World Series roster. But the team's current longest-tenured player also knows that it may be beyond his control, depending on MLB postseason roster rules. Woodruff, who underwent shoulder surgery during the 2025 season, has not pitched since July 4 after experiencing another issue with his shoulder. Woodruff was initially scheduled for season-ending surgery, but that was canceled when he showed signs of improvement. He began a throwing program in late August and threw off a mound during each of the Brewers' first two postseason series. He threw about two dozen live pitches Tuesday to teammates. "It went as good as it could have gone," Woodruff said Thursday. "And I've probably made their decision a little bit harder, which is a good problem for them. So, I'm lucky, I'm blessed. We got a chance to win the World Series and regardless of what happens, I will be just as excited to win if I'm on the roster or not." MLB rules say that a player on a postseason roster can be replaced only if he suffers an acute, non-chronic injury or ailment. If Woodruff were to suffer another injury, the Brewers are not sure if it would be considered recurring or pre-existing, which would prevent them from replacing Woodruff on the World Series roster. Several reports indicate the Brewers have discussed the situation with MLB. "We have a decision to make," Brewers president of baseball operations Matt Arnold said Thursday. "Still going to spend some minutes talking about him and again the rest of our group there." "This is a guy that's one of the most successful, dominant big-game pitchers I've ever been around, and there are also some rule constraints that we're having to work through with the health, etc., that have to be a consideration because he hasn't pitched in a game since July 4," Arnold said. Woodruff, 33, is 55-30 with a 3.10 ERA since debuting with the Brewers in 2017. At the end of last season, he took a $10 million buyout after declining his half of a mutual option, but then accepted the Brewers' $22.025 million, one-year qualifying offer. Woodruff made six starts in March and April this season before going on the injured list with right shoulder inflammation. In his first start back on June 22, he allowed one hit over six scoreless innings with 10 strikeouts in a no-decision against the Cincinnati Reds. The Brewers won 2-1 in 10 innings. In his third start after returning, he exited after allowing three runs in 3 2/3 innings against the Arizona Diamondbacks on July 4. There was a noticeable drop in his velocity. Brewers manager Pat Murphy said that he obviously would like to have Woodruff on the roster, but he balances that desire with what gives the club the best chance to win. "Now he's got a clean bill of health according to the trainers, but if that same injury comes up again, then we can't replace him," Murphy said. "So those are the things we've got to weigh heavily. What is he going to give us? We'd love to do it. It's a great story. But we have responsibility to those 20-some guys in there and to the organization and to the city and to whoever else we're responsible to." For Woodruff, his first World Series opportunity after nine seasons is down to wait and see. "I just wanted to be an option at this point," Woodruff said. "I know what I bring to the table as a player and I'll always believe in myself. But I also realized that I haven't pitched in a game in three months or whatever it is. So, there's definitely a lot that goes into the decision. I haven't heard anything yet. I'm sure they're going to talk about it obviously through (Thursday)." --Jim Hoehn, Field Level Media

item.title: Venezuelans call for elections in first national protest in nearly two years
item.description: Thousands of Venezuelans took to the streets on Thursday in the first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years, as demonstrators demanded free elections and other political changes with a notably thin presence of security forces.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thousands of Venezuelans took to the streets on Thursday in the first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years, as demonstrators demanded free elections and other political changes with a notably thin presence of security forces. The United States has been working closely with the interim government led by acting President Delcy Rodriguez since US forces captured President Nicolas Maduro in January. Both US President Donald Trump and Rodriguez, Maduro's former deputy, have said there will be elections, but have not set a date either for a legislative vote or a national contest for president. Opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize winner Maria Corina Machado, who has been outside the country for nearly a year after living in hiding following a contested 2024 election, has said elections must take place by July 2027. Her Vente Venezuela movement organized the protest, which took place in the capital Caracas and other cities, including Valencia, Maracay, San Cristobal and Maracaibo. “Seeing this makes me happy because I know change is possible," said 18-year-old cosmetology student Leosmary Hernandez, as she gathered with hundreds of others in northern Maracay. "I’ve been through so many hardships, so many problems because of the dollar, and difficulties studying. I have high hopes for my country and for our next leader, president, Maria Corina." "I went out to protest before, when things were much tougher, and I’m even less afraid today because I want my voice to be heard,” she added as music boomed around protesters waving Venezuelan flags. Venezuela's socialist movement, in power since 1999 under late President Hugo Chavez and then Maduro, has in the past [USN:KBN1DU1MZ TEXT:"deployed security forces against protesters"] decrying political repression, dizzying inflation, poor public services and other problems in the economically battered country, including after the 2024 presidential election. Security forces had minimal presence at protest sites on Thursday, and in many smaller cities demonstrators dispersed before dark. The ruling Socialist Party called for its supporters to march from Caracas' Plaza Venezuela, the same place the opposition planned to gather two hours later, to a location near the presidential palace to commemorate Breast Cancer Awareness Month. Interior Minister Diosdado Cabello, known for his close ties to the security services, was pictured on state television attending the march, while the opposition supporters moved their protest to a nearby location. NEGOTIATIONS CONTINUE US-backed talks between a faction of the opposition and the interim government, aimed at remaking the top court and the electoral council with an eye toward ensuring fairness at eventual elections, held their latest session this month, but changes could [USN:L1N45G0XU TEXT:"take significant time"]. The negotiations do not include Machado's political movement, though she has said she will not stand in the way of their progress. Machado's proxy roundly won the 2024 election according to vote tallies released by the opposition. But the government, which never released full counts, backed Maduro, as did the country's legal and electoral institutions. "We want presidential elections now. We want an electoral timetable to be announced now. We are not going to wait until 2028," said Maria Debora Marin, 57, who runs a clothing store in central Valencia, referring to rumors elections may only take place the year after next. "What we want is to move forward and finally get out of this nightmare." Amid the arrests of some of her closest collaborators, Machado went into hiding. Her last [USN:L1N3O40ZB TEXT:"public appearance in Venezuela"] was at protests to mark Maduro's third inauguration in January 2025, where she was briefly detained. Machado has for years sought US support, [USN:L4N3W51LU TEXT:"aligning with hawks"] in the Trump team who argued that Maduro — through links to drug gangs — represented a direct threat to US national security. Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, are facing [USN:L6N46017G TEXT:"drug and torture charges"] in the US. They have pleaded not guilty. But Trump has repeatedly praised Rodriguez's management and her willingness to [USN:L6N46308A TEXT:"welcome US investors"], saying last month it is too soon to consider elections. Machado's desire to return home, especially after [USN:L6N43414H TEXT:"devastating twin earthquakes"] in June, has caused [USN:L1N42Y0X4 TEXT:"friction in Washington"], with US officials asking her to delay her trip, Reuters has reported. "We're in limbo," said recent graduate Rayeska Puesme, 18, as she attended the protest in Caracas, adding she had considered leaving because of a lack of opportunities. "The United States removed one big problem, which was Maduro, but the rest are still there." "I feel in my heart that things are going to change, but I don't see when." Demonstrators were also calling for the release of prisoners they say are held for political reasons. Legal rights group Foro Penal, which represents opposition figures and others who have been detained, often on charges like treason, says there are still more than 320 political prisoners in Venezuela, despite releases that took place under an amnesty law backed by the legislature earlier this year. The government has repeatedly denied holding political prisoners and says the amnesty is generous.

item.title: Bradesco tem lucro líquido de R$7,1 bi no 3º tri, aprova recompra de ações
item.description: O Bradesco teve lucro líquido recorrente de R$7,1 bilhões no terceiro trimestre, alta de 14,6% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado, em linha com as previsões no mercado, com o presidente-executivo do banco, Marcelo Noronha, apontando um mercado de crédito mais restrito, com a taxa de juros em nível elevado e desaceleração da economia.
item.dc:creator: Paula Arend Laier
item.content:encoded: O Bradesco (BBDC3.SA) teve lucro líquido recorrente de R$7,1 bilhões no terceiro trimestre, alta de 14,6% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado, em linha com as previsões no mercado, com o presidente-executivo do banco, Marcelo Noronha, apontando um mercado de crédito mais restrito, com a taxa de juros em nível elevado e desaceleração da economia. O banco também anunciou um novo programa de [USN:L1N4681ED TEXT:"recompra"] de ações envolvendo 3,55% das ações ordinárias e aproximadamente 1% dos papéis preferenciais em circulação. O Bradesco também afirmou que aprovou R$4,1 bilhões em juros sobre capital próprio aos acionistas no terceiro trimestre. "É cenário desafiador para todos", afirmou o executivo em comunicado à imprensa, após a divulgação do balanço nesta quinta-feira. "Vimos nossas receitas relacionadas a crédito crescerem menos, mas conseguimos compensá-las com receitas não oriundas de crédito e bom controle de despesas”, acrescentou. Na comparação trimestral, o lucro do Bradesco subiu apenas 0,8%. A carteira de crédito da instituição totalizou R$1,15 trilhão no final de setembro, aumento de 11,1% ano a ano, mas de apenas 1,1% em relação ao final de junho. O índice de inadimplência acima de 90 dias no terceiro trimestre ficou em 4,6%, de 4,1% um ano antes e 4,3% no segundo trimestre de 2026. O custo do crédito, representado pela despesa de provisões (PDD) expandida, cresceu 24,3% ano a ano e 6,6% na comparação trimestral, para R$10,6 bilhões. O banco atribuiu a "leve alta" na inadimplência acima de 90 dias no trimestre ao segmento de micro, pequenas e médias empresas (MPME), particularmente nas operações de capital de giro com garantia do Governo Federal, afirmando que os atrasos desse produto corresponderam a cerca de metade da evolução da inadimplência total. Também destacou atrasos sazonais nas operações do Banco John Deere, que pressionaram os indicadores de pessoas físicas. Na movimentação da carteira de crédito por estágios, o montante no estágio 1, considerado com risco saudável, de até 30 dias, somava R$730,8 bilhões, enquanto no estágio 2, que mostram aumento de risco, com atrasos entre 31 e 90 dias; totalizava R$46,7 bilhões e no estágio 3, que indica problemas de recuperação de crédito; alcançava R$62,5 bilhões. No segundo trimestre do ano, esses valores eram R$727,3 bilhões, R$46 bilhões e R$60,2 bilhões, respectivamente. CONTROLE DE DESPESAS No terceiro trimestre, o retorno sobre o patrimônio líquido médio (ROAE) ficou em 15,6%, de 14,7% no mesmo intervalo do ano passado e 16,2% no segundo trimestre do ano. Desconsiderando o [USN:L1N45O0VZ TEXT:"aumento de capital"] de R$10 bilhões homologado no começo de outubro, o ROAE foi de 16,1%. O aumento de capital ajudou na melhora dos índices de capital do banco. O Bradesco encerrou o terceiro trimestre com índice de Basileia total de 16% e de capital principal de 12,1%. Um ano antes esses percentuais eram 15,9% e 11,4%, respectivamente. Em junho, eram 15,5% e 11,3%. As receitas totais do banco somaram R$38 bilhões, alta de 8,4% ano a ano, com a margem financeira total somando quase R$21,4 bilhões, expansão de 14,2% na mesma base de comparação. A margem com clientes cresceu 10,1%, para 20,5 bilhões, enquanto a margem com mercado alcançou R$875 milhões, de R$99 milhões um ano antes. As despesas operacionais recuaram 1%. O índice de eficiência ficou em 45,4%, de 50,1% no mesmo período do ano passado. Ao final de setembro, o banco tinha uma rede com 1.741 agências, além de 723 unidades de negócios e 1.428 postos de atendimento. Em junho, eram 1.844 agências, além de 698 unidades de negócios e 1.565 postos de atendimento. O resultado do grupo segurador do Bradesco mostrou lucro líquido recorrente de R$2,9 bilhões, alta de 14,1% ano a ano, com ROAE de 22%.

item.title: Ator Tom Skerritt, protagonista de “Alien” e “Top Gun”, morre aos 93 anos
item.description: O versátil ator Tom Skerritt, que estrelou grandes sucessos de Hollywood, incluindo o clássico de ficção científica “Alien”, a comédia de guerra “M.A.S.H” e o drama de ação “Top Gun”, faleceu aos 93 anos, confirmou seu empresário.
item.dc:creator: Will Dunham
item.content:encoded: O versátil ator Tom Skerritt, que estrelou grandes sucessos de Hollywood, incluindo o clássico de ficção científica “Alien”, a comédia de guerra “M.A.S.H” e o drama de ação “Top Gun”, faleceu aos 93 anos, confirmou seu empresário. Natural de Detroit, Skerritt, cuja carreira em Hollywood se estendeu da década de 1960 até a década de 2020, faleceu na quarta-feira de causas naturais, informou a ABC7, citando um comunicado da família do ator. Conhecido por sua beleza rude e pela capacidade de se destacar em diversos gêneros, Skerritt desempenhou atuações memoráveis em papéis principais e coadjuvantes no cinema e na televisão. O papel que marcou a carreira de Skerritt foi o de um cirurgião rebelde do Exército dos EUA na comédia de humor negro “M.A.S.H”, de 1970, do diretor Robert Altman, sobre a Guerra da Coreia -- filme cujo elenco também contava com Donald Sutherland, Elliott Gould e Sally Kellerman. Skerritt interpretou o sulista Duke Forrest enquanto os médicos do Hospital Cirúrgico Móvel do Exército atendiam soldados feridos. O filme, cuja popularidade coincidiu com o mal-estar dos norte-americanos em relação à Guerra do Vietnã, foi indicado a cinco prêmios do Oscar. No claustrofóbico filme de ficção científica e terror “Alien”, de 1979, dirigido por Ridley Scott, Skerritt interpretou Dallas, o capitão de uma nave espacial malfadada cuja tripulação se depara com uma criatura extraterrestre parasita mortal, de aparência surrealista e atitude hostil. Em uma das cenas mais famosas e sangrentas do filme, o personagem de Skerritt está sentado ao lado de seu colega de elenco John Hurt quando um bebê alienígena sai violentamente do torso do personagem de Hurt. “Alien”, uma obra-prima influente cujo elenco também contava com Sigourney Weaver e Ian Holm, recebeu duas indicações ao Oscar. “São a espontaneidade e o impulso que fazem a diferença, e foi isso que senti que tivemos em ‘Alien’. Cada um de nós tinha essa sintonia imediata uns com os outros -- o respeito que eu tinha pelos outros atores e o respeito que eles tinham por mim”, disse Skerritt ao entrevistador Peter Sobczynski em 2019, ao mesmo tempo em que elogiava a genialidade de Scott como diretor. “Alien” foi um dos vários filmes em que Skerritt atuou e que apresentavam personagens femininas fortes, neste caso a corajosa Ripley, interpretada por Weaver. Isso foi considerado pioneiro na época. “Quando li o roteiro, uma das coisas que mais gostei foi que a mulher se torna a heroína. Adorei isso”, disse Skerritt. “Ver mulheres em posições de força e determinação para estabelecer as conexões certas e tomar as decisões corretas foi o que me atraiu. Eu também vivenciei isso em ‘Flores de Aço’, com as mulheres daquele filme. Gostei da ideia de mulheres serem duronas, fortes e influentes.” Em “Flores de Aço” (1989), Skerritt interpretou Drum Eatenton, marido de M’Lynn Eatenton, personagem de Sally Field. Tony Scott, irmão do diretor de “Alien”, escalou Skerritt para o importante papel coadjuvante do instrutor da aviação naval Viper Metcalf no sucesso de bilheteria de 1986 “Top Gun”, que ajudou o astro Tom Cruise a alçar voo rumo à estratosfera de Hollywood. Skerritt também interpretou o marido de Shirley MacLaine no drama de balé “Momento de Decisão”, de 1977, dirigido por Herbert Ross, e contracenou com outra estrela em ascensão, Brad Pitt, no drama de época “Nada É Para Sempre”, de 1992, dirigido por Robert Redford e com belíssimas imagens. Entre outros filmes em que atuou, destacam-se: “Ensina-me a Viver” (1971), “Castelos de Gelo” (1978), “Na Hora Da Zona Morta” (1983), “Poltergeist 3 - O Capítulo Final” (1988), “Contato” (1997), “Lágrimas do Sol” (2003) e “Ted” (2012). Nascido em 25 de agosto de 1933, em Detroit, Skerritt serviu na Força Aérea dos Estados Unidos antes de se tornar ator, fazendo sua estreia no cinema em 1962 ao lado de um jovem Redford em “Obsessão de Matar”. Ele era pai de cinco filhos e se casou três vezes.

item.title: Trump invokes Cold War-era Defense Production Act for oil production, refining
item.description: US President Donald Trump determined on Thursday that petroleum production, refining, and related activities are essential to national defense, a move that could open up US funding for fossil fuel projects.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump determined on Thursday that petroleum production, refining, and related activities are essential to national defense, a move that could open up US funding for fossil fuel projects. In a presidential memo, Trump also invoked part of the Cold War-era Defense Production Act, allowing him to provide financial incentives for oil-related activities, pipelines and storage of liquid fuels. Prices for crude oil and [USN:L6N45Z19G TEXT:"diesel"] have surged since the US and Israel attacked Iran in joint action at the end of February. Since then, the conflict has limited energy shipments globally, with Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries exacerbating the fuel shortages. The surge in costs poses a risk for Trump in the November 3 elections, as his fellow Republicans try to maintain control of both chambers of Congress. The Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll that closed Monday shows [USN:L6N465159 TEXT:"just 36% of Americans"] approve of Trump's handling of the economy. The memo said that without taking the actions, the US is not able to provide enough of those energy services in a "timely manner due to constrained financing, long lead times, permitting and infrastructure bottlenecks, and supply chain limitations." The memo did not mention specific projects that could be funded. The US averaged around 13.6 million barrels of daily crude production in 2025, making it the largest crude producer worldwide. Last week, Vice President [USN:L6N45Z1BU TEXT:"JD Vance said"] the administration would use the Defense Production Act to expand capacity of a Texas refinery owned by Delek US Holdings (DK.N) Trump signed legislation last year that included $1 billion in Defense Production Act funding for energy-related projects deemed critical to national security.

item.title: Steelers scrap Paris fan event as Saints game proceeds despite protests
item.description: The Pittsburgh Steelers cancelled a weekend fan event in Paris on Thursday as French authorities prepared for fresh protests ahead of the NFL's first regular-season game in the capital.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Daheron, Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: The Pittsburgh Steelers cancelled a weekend fan event in Paris on Thursday as French authorities prepared for fresh protests ahead of the NFL's first regular-season game in the capital. France experienced some of its worst urban unrest in years [USN:L8N4670KY TEXT:"last weekend"], prompting President Emmanuel Macron to tighten curbs on protests [USN:L6N4680S7 TEXT:"on Thursday"], amid fears that demonstrations planned for Saturday could turn violent. The Steelers face the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis on Sunday, around 10 kilometres from the Place de la Bastille, where Saturday's protests are expected to begin. The Steelers informed fans on Thursday that a "Steelers House" fan event in the Bastille neighbourhood would not go forward. "The NFL, as they do for every game, including international games, is working closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. As stated by the NFL, there have been no disruptions or impacts at League sites," the team said in a statement. "As a precautionary measure, the Steelers designated bar that had been planned in Bastille – an area that has experienced recent disruptions – will not proceed." The Saints were practising this week in Versailles after arriving in France on Monday, while the Steelers were reportedly travelling to Paris on Thursday evening. "A lot of planning, a lot of extra conversations," Steelers coach Mike McCarthy told reporters on Wednesday. "Just because all the state of what surrounds the game." The French Interior Ministry was due to hold a press conference on Friday to outline security measures for the protests on Saturday. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell told reporters on Wednesday that he had been in contact with the US Secretary of State regarding security plans. "We're continuing to make sure we have all available information, make sure the appropriate steps are being made," said Goodell. "We're guests in the country. We're going to be good guests." The Paris game is one of a record nine international contests for the NFL this season, as the league looks to capitalise on lucrative overseas markets. League officials sought to ease concerns at a two-day owners meeting in New York this week, and [USN:L6N46612U TEXT:"told reporters"] that staging the game would not divert local security forces from other duties.

item.title: Tesoro retira a Venezuela de lista de países sujetos a restricciones inversión EEUU en el extranjero
item.description: El Departamento del Tesoro anunció el jueves una propuesta de normativa para controlar las inversiones en China, Rusia y otros países, una lista en la que no aparece Venezuela ahora que el expresidente Nicolás Maduro ya no está en el poder.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal
item.content:encoded: El Departamento del Tesoro anunció el jueves una propuesta de normativa para controlar las inversiones en China, Rusia y otros países, una lista en la que no aparece Venezuela ahora que el expresidente Nicolás Maduro ya no está en el poder. La Ley Integral de Seguridad Nacional en materia de Inversiones en el Extranjero de 2025 (COINS Act), aprobada por el Congreso en diciembre, supuso una ampliación significativa de los controles sobre las inversiones en el extranjero al exigir a las empresas y particulares que notifiquen al Tesoro determinados planes de inversión. Amplió la lista de países afectados e incluyó la biotecnología como uno de los sectores restringidos, otorgando al Tesoro la autoridad para añadir sectores adicionales según sea necesario. El programa de inversiones en el extranjero se centraba inicialmente solo en China, pero la legislación COINS amplió la lista de países "que suscitan preocupación" para incluir a Cuba, Irán, Corea del Norte, Rusia y Venezuela "bajo el régimen de Nicolás Maduro". Sin embargo, el Tesoro afirmó que había excluido a Venezuela debido a que el Gobierno de Maduro "ya no existe", añadiendo que el Gobierno de la presidenta encargada Delcy Rodríguez no se ajustaba a la definición. La norma propuesta podría seguir aplicándose a determinadas inversiones en entidades venezolanas, señaló el Tesoro, sin dar más detalles. El presidente Donald Trump ha adoptado un enfoque menos restrictivo respecto a las tecnologías chinas en su segundo mandato, pero la publicación el jueves de las normas propuestas podría indicar un deseo de mantener cierta presión sobre las ambiciones tecnológicas de Pekín. El Tesoro señaló que las normas propuestas no prohibirían todas las inversiones en países que suscitan preocupación. En cambio, se centrarían en inversiones específicas en entidades dedicadas a tecnologías de doble uso que beneficien a programas militares, a Estados que practican la vigilancia y a países donde se cometen abusos contra los derechos humanos. El Tesoro añadió un sector adicional —la biotecnología— a los cinco identificados en la legislación: semiconductores avanzados y microelectrónica; sistemas de inteligencia artificial; tecnologías de información cuántica; computación de alto rendimiento y supercomputación; y sistemas hipersónicos. Señaló que ciertas biotecnologías avanzadas podrían suponer un grave riesgo para la seguridad nacional, citando la proliferación de armas biológicas, el desarrollo de interfaces cerebro-ordenador y el perjuicio para la seguridad de la cadena de suministro de EEUU. Las normas no incluyen los posibles acuerdos de licencia celebrados por empresas farmacéuticas estadounidenses con China, afirmó un responsable del Tesoro, lo que satisface una exigencia clave de grandes fabricantes de medicamentos como Pfizer (PFE.N) .

item.title: Trump invoca ley de la época de la Guerra Fría para la producción y refinado de petróleo
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, determinó el jueves que la producción y el refinado de petróleo, así como las actividades relacionadas, son esenciales para la defensa nacional.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, determinó el jueves que la producción y el refinado de petróleo, así como las actividades relacionadas, son esenciales para la defensa nacional. Trump también invocó la Ley de Producción de Defensa, de la época de la Guerra Fría, que le permite ofrecer incentivos económicos para esas actividades relacionadas con el petróleo, así como para oleoductos y almacenamiento de energía.

item.title: US Democratic senator probes Ukraine's loss of Starshield service
item.description: Democratic US Senator Richard Blumenthal on Thursday said he had opened an inquiry into Ukraine's loss of critical access to the Pentagon's Starshield satellite communications service and the resulting degrading of Kyiv's ability to defend itself against Russian attacks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Democratic US Senator Richard Blumenthal on Thursday said he had opened an inquiry into Ukraine's loss of critical access to the Pentagon's Starshield satellite communications service and the resulting degrading of Kyiv's ability to defend itself against Russian attacks. "In the late evening of October 13, Ukrainian forces lost critical access to Starshield, the military-grade counterpart to SpaceX’s Starlink network, after their access to speeds at which equipment could stay connected to the network was capped," Blumenthal wrote in a letter to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. "The episode raises urgent questions about who possesses the technical and legal authority to alter these capabilities" and whether the Pentagon has "sufficient alternatives" if SpaceX-provided services become unavailable, Blumenthal wrote. Blumenthal is the senior Democrat on the Senate's Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations. He is seeking information on whether the change in service was [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"directed by the White House"], the Department of Defense or SpaceX. Republicans control the Senate, so Democrats lack subpoena power. Blumenthal can only request information and briefings from officials within and outside the government. He said the move put Ukrainian forces and civilians at risk and raised concerns "about who controls critical capabilities the US government has spent billions of dollars to procure." WEAKENED UKRAINE DEFENSES The Pentagon is the biggest customer of Starshield, which is the military-grade version of the Starlink service. A Pentagon spokesperson said: "As with all congressional correspondence, the Department will respond directly to the authors." Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy on October 14 said Elon Musk's SpaceX had [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"restricted Starlink services"], weakening Ukraine's air defenses. The controversy came as the Trump administration was pressuring Kyiv to halt its attacks on Russian energy infrastructure and encouraging Russia to return to negotiations over ending its war in Ukraine. Blumenthal told Hegseth the Senate panel will look into government interactions with and reliance on SpaceX technology. He set deadlines of November 5 for responses to questions embedded in the letter to Hegseth, and November 12 for a briefing by SpaceX officials with knowledge of the Starshield restriction. Besides this latest inquiry, Blumenthal has been trying to investigate [USN:L6N45E0PR TEXT:"a series of actions related to the Trump administration"], including contracts negotiated for building a White House ballroom at an estimated cost of $400 million and Trump-linked crypto firms. If Democrats win control of the Senate in November 3 midterm elections, he likely would become chairman of the investigations panel.

item.title: US Treasury drops Venezuela from countries facing outbound US investment restrictions
item.description: The US Treasury Department on Thursday announced proposed rules for screening outbound investment in China, Russia and other countries, a list that no longer includes Venezuela now that the country's former president Nicolas Maduro is not in power.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal
item.content:encoded: The US Treasury Department on Thursday announced proposed rules for screening outbound investment in China, Russia and other countries, a list that no longer includes Venezuela now that the country's former president Nicolas Maduro is not in power. Treasury will accept comments through December 7 on the proposed rules, which were mandated under the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act of 2025, or COINS Act, that [USN:L1N3XN0X2 TEXT:"passed Congress in December"], but grew out of a bipartisan effort first begun under former President Joe Biden in 2023. The COINS Act marked a significant expansion of US outbound investment controls, requiring US firms and individuals to notify Treasury about certain investment plans while banning them outright in other cases to prevent harm to US national security. It expanded the covered countries and added biotechnology as one of the restricted sectors, giving Treasury the authority to add additional sectors as needed. The outbound program initially targeted China alone, but the COINS legislation expanded the list of countries "of concern" to include Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela "under the regime of Nicolas Maduro." But Treasury said it dropped Venezuela since Maduro's government "no longer exists" following the capture of the former president by US forces in January, adding that the current government, led by Maduro's deputy, Delcy Rodriguez, did not meet the definition. The proposed rule could still apply to certain investments in Venezuelan entities, Treasury said, without elaborating. President Donald Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping for a lavish state visit to Washington last month, and has pursued a less restrictive approach on Chinese technologies in his second term, but Thursday's release of the proposed rules may signal a desire to keep some pressure on Beijing's tech ambitions. "The idea behind the outbound program is to ensure that we have the ability to monitor and potentially prohibit the types of investments" that pose risks to US national security, Treasury Assistant Secretary Chris Pilkerton, who oversees investment security issues, told Reuters. "It's not just about the investment itself; it's not just about the money. It's about the network, the supply chain, and things like that that come from that investment," he said, adding that such a complex web of relationships would be hard to regulate otherwise through export controls or other measures. Treasury said the proposed rules would not ban all investments in countries of concern. Instead, they would target specific investments in entities that engaged in dual-use technologies that benefited military programs, surveillance states and countries with human-rights abuses. The proposed rules require notification about prospective investments in six sectors and five designated countries, while banning them outright in the case of artificial intelligence. They allow certain exceptions, including investments in publicly traded companies and transactions valued at less than $50,000. The proposal would also allow investors to request exemptions for transactions deemed to be in the national interest of the United States, Treasury said. Treasury also added an additional sector -- biotechnology -- to the five identified in the legislation: advanced semiconductors and microelectronics; artificial intelligence systems; quantum information technologies; high-performance computing and supercomputing; and hypersonic systems. It said certain advanced biotechnologies could pose an acute risk to national security, citing the proliferation of biological weapons, the development of brain-computer interfaces and harm to US supply chain security. The rules do not include potential licensing agreements made by [USN:L1N4570SO TEXT:"US pharmaceutical companies "]with China, a Treasury official said, meeting a key demand of major drugmakers like Pfizer (PFE.N) . The proposed rules ban investments in artificial intelligence technologies in the target countries. Treasury said it decided on the ban given rapid advances over the past two years that raised questions about the efficacy of "regulating or even distinguishing the most advanced models."

item.title: Australia weigh changes for Cape Town decider after South Africa rout
item.description: Australia will have some hard decisions to make over the weekend as they lick their wounds after a bruising loss in the second test against South Africa and consider their line-up for the series-deciding clash next week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia will have some hard decisions to make over the weekend as they lick their wounds after a bruising loss in the second test against South Africa and consider their line-up for the series-deciding clash next week. Defeat by an innings and 31 runs in Gqeberha has left several players’ places in jeopardy and given the selectors plenty to ponder before the third test starts in Cape Town on Tuesday. Australia are not known for making knee-jerk changes after a defeat, and captain Pat Cummins was circumspect on the topic after the loss at St George’s Park. "It's always that delicate balance," he said of a potential switch in personnel. "Do you feel like someone's just about to turn the corner and they're going to be away? Or does it now feel like the right time for change? So that's what will be spoken about in the next few days. "We'll probably have Cam Green and Josh Inglis available for next week. I'm sure their names will get thrown around when we try to work out an eleven," he told reporters on Thursday. The debate is likely to include Marnus Labuschagne, who has scored 37 twice, 14 and 39 in his four innings in the two tests in South Africa this month. He has not made a test century since scoring 111 against England at Old Trafford in July 2023. "The hardest thing about opening or batting No. 3 is actually getting yourself in. So he's actually doing the hard bit. He's getting to thirties," Cummins added. "He's got to find a way to turn those into bigger scores. Thirties aren't going to win you too many matches. "It's certainly not a technique error. It's maybe some decisions where the game demands something a little bit different. We'll work on that. He's hitting the ball well,” added the skipper. CHANGE IN BATTING ORDER There is likely to be a shift in the batting order with Matt Renshaw fancied to return to the top in place of Nic Maddinson, allowing Green to return from an abdominal strain. Josh Inglis and Cooper Connolly are also options. "Looking around the changing room at how good our batters are and the standards they all hold themselves to, I think we're probably a little bit short of where we'd like to be. We've got three or four days to get it right for Cape Town. There'll be lots of conversations." Veteran spinner Nathan Lyon could also be recalled, depending on conditions, leaving Australia to decide how to accommodate Scott Boland, who took five wickets in the test and produced a heroic effort with the bat as he offered some second-innings resistance on Thursday. "We clearly need to be a lot better than that if we want to compete,” Cummins added. “I think a loss can sometimes kick you into gear. You can maybe paper over the cracks sometimes in a win. Whereas I think in a loss, it makes you ask questions as a player of yourself."

item.title: Trading Day: Maximum pAIn
item.description: A wave of worry around AI and tech crashed over global markets on Thursday, slamming equities and bond yields as investors sought the refuge of US Treasuries, while a spike in Brent crude oil to a five-month high and continued unrest in France also deepened the gloom.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded:
A wave of worry around [USN:L6N468196 TEXT:"AI and tech"] crashed over global markets on Thursday, slamming [USN:L6N4680M6 TEXT:"equities"] and bond yields as investors sought the refuge of US Treasuries, while a spike in Brent crude [USN:L6N4671H6 TEXT:"oil "]to a five-month high and continued unrest in [USN:L6N4680QK TEXT:"France "]also deepened the gloom. In [USN:L6N46713L TEXT:"my column today"], I look at whether the US Treasury will reduce the size of 20-year bond auctions, or soon scrap them all together. Interest payments are high, Treasury wants to shorten the maturity of the debt, and the 20-year part of the curve is relatively illiquid. Absent concerted fiscal tightening, Treasury may have to tinker round the edges if it wants to lower long-term yields. This could help. Bitcoin -4%, biggest fall since June. BONDS: [USN:L6N4680QK TEXT:"French/German"] 10y spread 175 bps, widest since 2011. US yields sink as much as 20 bps across the curve. 5-year TIPS auction soft - lowest bid/cover since April last year, highest yield in three years. COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:L6N4671H6 TEXT:"Oil "]up as much as 4%, Brent highest since May above $112. [USN:L4N46801E TEXT:"Gold "]-2%, lowest in more than two months.

Today's Talking Points: Call security Investors' AI fears ramped up on Thursday, and not just for the usual concerns around spend, revenue and valuations. On top of all that, the global scramble by companies and governments to patch critical flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet in response to millions of hacking attempts is a reminder of how vulnerable the world is to cybersecurity breaches and AI going rogue. When governments take websites offline as an emergency precaution, you know it's serious. "I've not seen anything like this in a long, long time," Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said. The good news is these flaws appear to have been flagged by AI before any serious or lasting damage could be wrought. The iShares Cybersecurity and Tech ETF (with the appropriate ticker symbol ) rose on Thursday, bringing its year-to-date gains up to nearly 50%. Play it safe There's been a lot of talk this year that the assets investors typically turn to in periods of market turbulence - particularly US Treasuries and other sovereign bonds - have lost their safe-haven allure. They are no longer the hedge or portfolio diversifier they used to be. There is probably some truth to that, but there's life in the old dogs yet. German bund yields had their biggest drop since May last year, and the Japanese yen and Swiss franc were the two biggest climbers in global FX markets on Thursday. The move in US Treasuries was extraordinary, as yields plunged across the curve and by as much as 20 basis points. And that was despite Brent oil spiking to $112 a barrel. Granted, gold fell, but when was the last time gold truly behaved like a "safe haven"? Bearing up China's stock market fall on Thursday means the blue-chip CSI300 index is now down more than 20% from its most recent closing peak on June 22. That's a bear market. Others might argue Chinese stocks have been in a bear market for nearly two decades, since the all-time high reached in 2007. But however you slice it, investing in China has been challenging, to put it mildly. The currency is rising and is now at a four-year high, while the 10-year bond yield is hovering around its all-time low below 1.60%. But the domestic woes of debt, deflation and depressed consumption weigh heavily. Foreign investment [USN:P8N42P008 TEXT:"flows"] into China in January-September fell 4.3% year-on-year to 548.8 billion yuan ($82.2 billion), the commerce ministry said on Thursday, while outbound non-financial direct investment totaled $101 billion. Export inflows are booming, investor inflows, not so much. What could move markets tomorrow?
